out.window: The qualifying event is the 2026 Russian parliamentary election, scheduled for September 2026; its official turnout must be known by October 31, 2027, at 11:59 PM ET. The rules specify neither exact polling dates nor a separate observation-window start. The most plausible intended start is market creation, whose date is not supplied, with qualification restricted to this election. This ambiguity has little practical effect because earlier elections cannot qualify.
out.qualifying_criteria: YES requires reported nationwide turnout for the 2026 Russian parliamentary election to be at least 47% and strictly below 50%, calculated as total votes cast divided by total eligible voters. Exactly 47% belongs to this bracket; exactly 50% belongs to the higher bracket. Official Russian government election results, particularly the Central Election Commission, are primary; consensus credible reporting may substitute if official results are unavailable. Polling intentions, turnout forecasts, mobilization plans, regional turnout and United Russia vote-share targets do not qualify. If results remain unknown at the deadline, the lowest bracket wins, implying NO for this bracket.
out.evidence_inside_window: No evidence reports qualifying 2026 election turnout. E1 and E2 describe pre-election forecasts and participation intentions, not votes cast. E3 describes planned workplace mobilization; E4 reports mobilization arrangements and party vote-share targets, neither of which establishes nationwide election turnout. E1–E4 concern preparations for the relevant election, although their position relative to market creation cannot be established. E5 reports 2021 turnout of 51.72% and E6 reports 2016 turnout of 47.88%; both are historical background outside the qualifying election window.
out.base_rate_for_change: There are 415 calendar days from the as_of date, September 11, 2026, to the reporting deadline, although the election is scheduled for the same month as the as_of date. The relevant process is one election producing a turnout result, rather than repeated opportunities for turnout to change over 415 days. Of the two historical parliamentary elections supplied, one landed in this bracket and one above it; that tiny sample provides a weak 50% historical frequency. E1's modeled forecast of 51–53%, the 2021 result of 51.72%, and intensified mobilization shift probability toward turnout above 50%. Allowing several percentage points of forecast uncertainty still leaves a meaningful chance of 47–50%, approximately one quarter.
out.key_uncertainty: How accurately VTsIOM's 51–53% forecast predicts the officially reported turnout, including whether stronger administrative mobilization raises participation as intended. Survey participation intentions are not directly comparable to realized turnout, and the file provides no historical forecast-error distribution. Official reported turnout is the settlement variable, so uncertainty about actual participation alone does not determine this market.
